caption: LUM-1318 paste folding on the landed marker model (LUM-1328 + the renumber fix). A 200-line bracketed paste becomes one `[paste #1 +200 lines]` marker and the composer stays one row; Enter hands the model the WHOLE pasted text (the transcript shows `pasted line 200`, never a marker); a second paste folds to the next id and deleting the first marker RENUMBERS the survivor down to `#1` while keeping its own payload — the next Enter submits the 11-line text, not the 200-line one; the last panel is the A/B: the same bytes delivered as individual key presses (no bracketed-paste markers) fold nothing and pile up as a 200-row draft. Real PTY at 100x30 driving the debug binary built from this commit.

panels.label: 3. Enter hands the model the whole pasted text: `pasted line 200` is in the transcript, no marker ever is

4. Up recalls the submitted prompt: the recalled draft carries the marker again (the registry travels with the history entry), so the draft stays short and still expands — never a marker with nothing behind it

5. Ctrl+C clears that recalled draft (`Clear` is the whole-draft chord; `Ctrl+U` is line-scoped since LUM-1312) — the grid is byte-identical to panel 3, which is the point: an empty composer and an untouched transcript
6. paste again after the clear: the id comes from the monotone counter (upstream never resets `pasteCounter`), so this draft's first marker is #2, not #1
